name: WA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Emily Randall running with a large fundraising edge
Republican Teresa Fox's minimal campaign resources
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Randall: a 10-point Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of roughly $1.2 million to $28,000, with no outside spending against her. Markets price her near 94%, and with no polls available the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of about 21 points.
model.watch: A polling surprise or a major late outside-spending intervention against Randall would be the main way this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent Emily Randall defends a western Washington district that leans Democratic by about 10 points. She has raised roughly $1.2 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican Teresa Fox has raised under $30,000 and shows no outside support. No independent groups are spending against Randall, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Randall about a 94% chance of winning. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided resource gap, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in November.
